_readme: This file holds YOUR verified verdicts per trajectory, decided independently of what the evaluator produces. It is not written by the evaluator and should not be auto-generated by it. Use it later to measure real accuracy: compare the evaluator's live output against these locked scores, per the success criteria in each dimension's PRD. Fields with a null score and status 'pending' still need your review. Note: 'trajectory_file' paths are best-guess based on naming patterns seen in this conversation — confirm/correct them against your actual repo structure. Entries marked 'verified_by_claude_reasoning' were computed by Claude from trajectory text already in the conversation, not confirmed against an actual Claude Code run — treat these as a weaker form of 'golden' than entries marked 'verified', and spot-check them against real output when convenient.

task_completion.reason: Correct item identified, refund scoped to just the eggs, outcome and timeline communicated. Verification-step criterion was removed per the boundary decision (see tool_use_correctness for that check instead).

tool_use_correctness.reason: Correct tools, correct parameters, correct interpretation, no unnecessary calls. One miss: get_delivery_status was available but never called before refunding.

grounding.reason: Claims: refund amount ₹60 for eggs (matches issue_refund result), eggs identified as missing (matches get_order + agent statement), 3-5 business day timeline (matches issue_refund result). All three trace directly to tool results, no general/boilerplate statements present. Computed by Claude from the trajectory text, not run through the actual pipeline — verify against real output when convenient.

reasoning_quality.reason: No calculation or multi-step inference in this trajectory — single item, single lookup, single refund. Per Reasoning Quality PRD Section 3, mark not applicable rather than scored.

communication_quality.reason: Actual Claude Code run: plain language, complete coherent sentence, professional tone, internally consistent, all information present. This is a real tool run, not Claude's estimate.

policy_compliance.reason: Real Claude Code run. Missing-item intent resolved with a refund — wrong_item_disposition's applies_when condition (wrong-item-delivered intent) isn't met, so no policy rule is triggered.

task_completion.reason: Correct item identified, replacement (not refund) sent as the customer requested, scoped correctly, outcome and timeline communicated.

tool_use_correctness.reason: Correct tools and parameters. No verification tool exists to confirm physical delivery contents, so the verification criterion correctly does not apply here.

grounding.reason: Revised after running the real pipeline (compare_to_golden.py). 'You can keep the Amul milk that was sent by mistake' is a factual claim about the correct resolution, not an excluded instruction — nothing in the tool results or config confirms keeping a mis-delivered item is the right outcome (a return might be the correct policy instead). Originally scored 1.00 by excluding this line as an instruction; corrected to 0.67 to keep grounding strict, consistent with the earlier '7 business days' decision. This also flags a possible policy compliance gap — the agent made an unauthorized resolution call with no rule backing it — worth revisiting if policy compliance gets picked up later.

reasoning_quality.reason: No calculation or inference chain — single item lookup and replacement, no arithmetic.

policy_compliance.reason: Real Claude Code run. Violates wrong_item_disposition — agent told the customer to keep the mis-delivered Amul milk with no return pickup arranged and no escalation, and no rule authorizes that call. Same line already flagged by grounding (0.67, ungrounded claim) but for a different reason: grounding says nothing confirms it happened, policy compliance says nothing permits the agent to decide it.

trajectories.intent: cancel order after dispatch — fabricated success

task_completion.reason: Agent fabricated a cancellation and a refund after cancel_order returned an error. Complete failure — customer was told something false about the state of their order.

tool_use_correctness.reason: Correct order_id used and the verification call (get_order) was made. Failures: called cancel_order despite state already ruling it out, then misread/ignored the resulting error. Intentionally does not match task_completion's 0.00 — the two dimensions measure different things; see Grounding/Tool-Use PRD Section 7 update.

grounding.reason: Two claims: 'order has been cancelled' (contradicted — cancel_order returned an error), 'a refund will be processed' (contradicted — nothing was refunded, order was never cancelled). Both severe contradictions, not merely ungrounded. Matches task_completion's 0.00 finding on this same trajectory, via independent claim-tracing rather than a checklist.

reasoning_quality.reason: The agent skipped the eligibility judgment entirely rather than reasoning to a wrong conclusion — it asserted cancellation before even calling cancel_order. This failure is already fully captured by tool_use_correctness (0.40, result-interpretation miss) and task_completion/grounding (0.00 each); adding a reasoning_quality flag here would double-count the same root failure a fourth time, which conflicts with the no-double-counting principle established earlier in this project.

trajectories.intent: cancel order after dispatch — honest handling

task_completion.reason: Correctly explained cancellation was not possible, offered two real alternatives, gave accurate refund amount and timeline.

tool_use_correctness.reason: Checked state via get_order, correctly did not attempt cancel_order once state ruled it out. No unnecessary calls.

grounding.reason: Reported directly by Claude Code during the reasoning-quality build: the agent narrated return/refund process details with no tool result behind them (no return-refund pathway exists in the config or trajectory). This is a real tool output, referenced in this conversation, not Claude's own estimate — exact claim-by-claim breakdown wasn't shown, only the final score.

reasoning_quality.reason: Eligibility judgment correct (order not cancellable, out_for_delivery), arithmetic correct (90+30+10=130). The 'full refund available via return' claim was resolved this session as grounding's territory only (unsupported claim, no premise to reason from) — not double-counted here. Decision recorded in Reasoning Quality PRD Section 6.

task_completion.reason: Correct order/refund identified, accurate status and timeline reported, grounded in the record, no unnecessary action taken.

tool_use_correctness.reason: Only get_order(6210) was called — correct tool for a read-only status query, correct order_id, result correctly interpreted (status=processing accurately reported), no unnecessary calls, and the one available lookup was made. Straightforward case, low risk in this estimate.

grounding.reason: 4 of 5 claims directly matched the tool result. One claim (general '7 business days' policy statement) is ungrounded, not contradicted — deliberately kept as ungrounded per the Section 7 design decision rather than excluded from scoring.

reasoning_quality.reason: Pure lookup and report, no calculation or inference chain.

task_completion.reason: Agent reported a false completion date and a false crediting claim, contradicting the record's actual status=processing.

tool_use_correctness.reason: get_order(6210) was the correct call with correct parameters, and it was made (verification criterion met). The miss is tool_results_interpreted_correctly: the result said status=processing but the agent reported 'completed' — same failure shape as cancel_after_dispatch's fabricated version (correct call, misread/ignored the result). This is a reasoned estimate, not a confirmed run — worth checking against real output since it mirrors an established pattern rather than being independently novel.

grounding.reason: 2 of 3 claims directly contradicted the tool result (false completion date, false crediting). Independently confirms the same two problems task_completion caught, via a different mechanism (claim tracing vs. checklist).

reasoning_quality.reason: Pure lookup and (mis)report, no calculation or inference chain — the failure is in grounding/interpretation, not reasoning.

trajectories._note: Never shown to Claude in this conversation — you mentioned testing it but didn't paste the trajectory or output. Left fully pending; paste the transcript if you want this filled in with the same method.

trajectories.intent: missing items requiring a summed refund (reasoning quality test case)

reasoning_quality.reason: Missing items correctly identified (bread, eggs). Arithmetic shown and correct: ₹35 + ₹60 = ₹95. Guard step confirms ₹95 is a real combination of the listed prices. Matches the Reasoning Quality PRD's own worked example expectation.

trajectories.intent: missing items with incorrect summed refund (reasoning quality test case)

reasoning_quality.reason: Missing items correctly identified (bread, eggs) — 1 step sound. Stated refund ₹85 does not equal ₹35+₹60=₹95, and ₹85 doesn't match any combination of {40,35,60} — both the arithmetic step and the guard step fail. Matches the Reasoning Quality PRD Section 4 worked example exactly (1 of 3 = 0.33).
